question.text: In van dar Wall equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>V</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow></mfenced><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mi>R</mi><mi>T</mi><mo>;</mo><mo> </mo><mi>P</mi></math> is pressure, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi></math> is volume, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is universal gas constant and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi></math> is temperature. The ratio of constants <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mfrac></math> is dimensionally equal to :

solution.text:
P+aV2V-b=nRT

Dimensions of b should be equal to dimensions of V. Similarly, dimensions of a will be equal to dimensions of PV2.

Therefore, dimensions of ab=PV2V=PV.
